root_cause.text: In the XFS `xlog_alloc_log` function, the `l_iclog_roundoff` field is incorrectly initialized to 512 bytes when the log stripe unit is unspecified, rather than using the actual log sector size (`sb_logsectsize`), causing alignment mismatches on 4k physical sector disks.
root_cause.evidence: The patch modifies `fs/xfs/xfs_log.c` to add a check for `mp->m_sb.sb_logsectsize > 0` before defaulting to `BBSIZE`, ensuring the roundoff factor matches the physical sector size (4096) instead of the hardcoded 512 bytes when `sb_logsunit` is 0.

agent_logs.evidence_points: The patch modifies `fs/xfs/xfs_log.c` to add a check for `mp->m_sb.sb_logsectsize > 0` to set `log->l_iclog_roundoff` to this value before defaulting to `BBSIZE`, addressing the mismatch between the assumed 512-byte roundoff and the actual 4096-byte sector size described in the CVE logs.

intent_record.intent_summary: Corrects log allocation rounding initialization by prioritizing sb_logsectsize over BBSIZE when sb_logsunit is not applicable.
intent_record.what: Inserted an else-if condition to check if mp->m_sb.sb_logsectsize is greater than zero within the xlog_alloc_log function.
intent_record.how: Sets log->l_iclog_roundoff to the log sector size when the primary logsunit condition fails but sector size is valid, preventing an immediate fallback to the default BBSIZE.

vuln_statements.explanation: This statement initializes l_iclog_roundoff to a hardcoded 512 bytes when the log stripe unit is unspecified. According to the root cause, this should use sb_logsectsize instead to ensure proper alignment on 4k physical sector disks. Using 512 bytes causes alignment mismatches on systems with larger sector sizes.
